description: The pie chart illustrates the distribution of mathematical problem types across different difficulty levels and topics, based on the Odyssey Math dataset. The largest segment, representing 21.19% (82 problems), is labeled "Algebra – University-level," depicted in dark blue. The second largest segment, "Algebra – High School," accounts for 17.83% (69 problems) and is shown in light red. Other significant segments include "Combinatorics – Olympiad-level" at 9.56% (37 problems, light green), "Geometry – Olympiad-level" at 6.46% (25 problems, orange), and "Linear Algebra and Abstract Algebra – University-level" at 6.20% (24 problems, pink). Smaller segments include "Pre-Calculus – High School" at 14.21% (55 problems, dark brown), "Geometry – High School" at 3.62% (14 problems, light purple), "Differential Equations – University-level" at 3.62% (14 problems, gray), "Probability – University-level" at 5.43% (21 problems, teal), and "Statistics – University-level" at 4.39% (17 problems, light blue). The chart visually emphasizes the dominance of university-level algebra problems, with the segments arranged in a clockwise order from the largest to the smallest, and each slice is labeled with its category, percentage, and total count.
